# Algebra generated by primitive parity-even Weyl sums: spectral separation criterion and level-one counterexample

**Proposal-only rigorous result, 23 November 2026.** This is a partial characterization, not an all-depth determination.

Let N=3^k and assume the standard odd-N Weyl system and exact Egorov quantization of T=A². Write D_N for the commutant of the quantum cat-map U_T. Let V_even be the span of the parity-even primitive orbit sums E_[q]=S_(O_q)+S_(O_-q), where q runs over units modulo N up to sign. Define B_N to be the unital *-algebra generated by these sums inside D_N.

## Theorem 1: spectral separation gives an exact finite criterion

Assume MF-185's simple-spectrum conclusion for U_T, so D_N is a commutative C*-algebra of dimension N. Let P_1,...,P_N be the rank-one spectral projections of U_T, and write

\[
E_{[q]}=\sum_{a=1}^N \lambda_{[q],a}P_a.
\]

The E_[q] are self-adjoint: every primitive T-orbit is antipodally invariant and W_x*=W_(-x). Hence all λ are real. Associate to each eigenline a joint signature

\[
\Lambda_a=(\lambda_{[q],a})_{[q]\in R^\times/\{\pm1\}}\in\mathbb R^{3^{k-1}}.
\]

Then B_N consists **exactly** of the diagonal operators whose eigenvalue is constant on each fiber of the signature map a↦Λ_a. In particular,

\[
\boxed{\dim B_N=\#\{\Lambda_1,\ldots,\Lambda_N\}\le N,}
\]

and B_N=D_N **if and only if** all N joint signatures are distinct.

**Proof.** Simultaneous diagonalization identifies D_N with C^N, with pointwise multiplication and conjugation. The unital *-algebra generated by real coordinate functions λ_[q] consists of functions constant on their common level sets. Conversely, if signatures Λ_a and Λ_b differ, some coordinate function separates them. For each distinct signature Λ, choose for each other signature Λ' one coordinate q(Λ') where they differ and form

\[
p_\Lambda(z)=\prod_{\Lambda'\ne\Lambda}
\frac{z_{q(\Lambda')}-\Lambda'_{q(\Lambda')}}{\Lambda_{q(\Lambda')}-\Lambda'_{q(\Lambda')}}.
\]

This polynomial equals 1 at Λ and 0 at every other signature. Evaluating it on the commuting generators produces the joint fiber projection. Therefore the generated algebra has one independent idempotent per distinct signature. QED.

## Theorem 2: level-one generated algebra is proper

At N=3, the primitive parity-even space has one generator

\[
E=\sum_{x\in(\mathbb Z/3)^2\setminus\{0\}}W_x.
\]

Direct Weyl multiplication gives E²=8I−2E, so B_3=span{I,E} has dimension 2. The full commutant D_3 has dimension 3 by MF-185 (or by the A² orbit count), hence

\[
\boxed{B_3\subsetneq D_3,\qquad\dim B_3=2<3.}
\]

In fact the minimal polynomial of E is (z−2)(z+4), so its two spectral values are 2 and −4, with multiplicities 2 and 1 respectively (Tr(E)=0, dimension 3). Thus the signatures fail to separate two cat-map eigenlines at N=3.

**Proof.** The Weyl sum E is self-adjoint. Its square identity is obtained by counting pairs x+y=z with the standard Weyl phase: for z=0 there are eight inverse pairs, and for z≠0 the coefficient is −2 (the remaining six nonzero ordered pairs have phase sum −2). The polynomial relation yields eigenvalues 2 and −4; trace zero gives multiplicities 2 and 1. Since E is nonscalar, I and E are linearly independent. The commutant dimension is three. QED.

## Theorem 3: exact Gram and moment reduction

The Hilbert–Schmidt Gram matrix of the parity-even generators is diagonal, with

\[
\operatorname{Tr}(E_{[q]}E_{[p]})=2NL\,\delta_{[q],[p]},\qquad L=4\cdot3^{k-1}.
\]

Moreover, every mixed trace moment Tr(E_[q1]⋯E_[qs]) is an explicitly finite cyclotomic sum over tuples of phase-space vectors x_i in the respective norm fibers, constrained by x_1+⋯+x_s=0. Therefore the joint signature multiset can in principle be reconstructed by exact moment computations, without relying on floating-point eigenvalue coincidences.

The Gram identity alone does **not** determine dim B_N: linear independence of generators is weaker than multiplicative generation of the full commutant.

## Remaining open target

Determine the number of distinct joint signatures for k>=2. A proof that all are distinct would show B_N=D_N for those levels; a collision gives a proper subalgebra. A reproducible exact cyclotomic or symbolic calculation at N=9 is the next discriminating test. Do not infer a general answer from the N=3 exception.

## Scope

This is a finite-dimensional spectral-algebra characterization conditional on the established MF-185 simple-spectrum and exact Egorov conventions. It neither makes a physical claim nor turns the shear Fourier projections into quantum channels.
